import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify potential drivers (clinical or cohort variables)
    clinical_features = [fid for fid, typ in zip(feats.ids, feats.types) if typ == 'clinical']
    
    # If no clinical features, try to find strong correlates
    if not clinical_features:
        # Look for features with highest effect sizes
        effect_sizes = []
        for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
            if feats.types[i] != 'derived':
                y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, i])
                y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, i])
                effect_sizes.append((abs(y1_mean - y0_mean), fid))
        effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
        clinical_features = [fid for _, fid in effect_sizes[:3]]  # Take top 3
    
    # Check if any clinical feature shows strong association with outcome
    best_driver = None
    max_effect = 0
    
    for fid in clinical_features:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, idx])
        y1_mean = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, idx])
        effect = abs(y1_mean - y0_mean)
        if effect > max_effect:
            max_effect = effect
            best_driver = fid
    
    # If no clear driver found or weak effect, return empty design
    if not best_driver or max_effect < 0.1:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build regression model with all features except near-duplicates
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    selected_features = set()
    feature_correlations = {}
    
    # Compute correlations between all pairs
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids):
            if i >= j:
                continue
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                feature_correlations[(fid1, fid2)] = corr
    
    # Create a mapping of features to their correlated partners
    correlation_map = defaultdict(set)
    for (fid1, fid2), _ in feature_correlations.items():
        correlation_map[fid1].add(fid2)
        correlation_map[fid2].add(fid1)
    
    # Select representative features avoiding near-duplicates
    used_features = set()
    for fid in feats.ids:
        if fid in used_features:
            continue
        # Add this feature and mark its correlated ones as used
        selected_features.add(fid)
        for correlated_fid in correlation_map[fid]:
            used_features.add(correlated_fid)
    
    # Build logistic regression with selected features
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_features]]
    lr = LogisticRegression(fit_intercept=True, penalty='l1', solver='liblinear')
    lr.fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Get coefficients and identify important features
    coefs = lr.coef_[0]
    feature_importance = [(abs(coef), fid) for coef, fid in zip(coefs, selected_features)]
    feature_importance.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Select top features for regression
    top_features = [fid for _, fid in feature_importance[:10]]
    
    # Return design with driver and selected features
    return Design(
        drivers=(best_driver,) if best_driver else (),
        columns=tuple(top_features),
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
